comments.content:
Making the batch order configurable breaks the boundary fix-up in the loop below, which still assumes DESC (newest-first) ordering.

In the result loop the code does:
- `if (i == 0 && original_refresh_window->end_isnull)` -> `range->end = ts_time_get_noend_or_max(...)`
- `if (i == (SPI_processed - 1) && original_refresh_window->start_isnull)` -> `range->start = ts_time_get_nobegin_or_min(...)`

With `refresh_newest_first == false` the list is ASC, so `i == 0` is the *oldest* batch and `i == SPI_processed - 1` is the *newest* one. For a typical policy with `end_offset => NULL` (`end_isnull == true`), the oldest batch would then be assigned `end = +infinity`, i.e. the very first batch refreshes the whole remaining window and batching is effectively defeated (and with a NULL `start_offset` the newest batch would start at `-infinity`). This is exactly the case exercised by the new test (`start_offset => 15 days, end_offset => NULL, refresh_newest_first => false`), but the test only compares row counts/data so it doesn't catch it.

The first/last index used by those two conditions must depend on the ordering.

comments.content: Passing `refresh_newest_first == false` through to `continuous_agg_split_refresh_window()` changes the SQL ordering to `ASC`, but that function's post-processing of open-ended windows still hard-codes the newest-first assumption: it overwrites the *end* of the first returned row with `ts_time_get_noend_or_max()` when `original_refresh_window->end_isnull`, and the *start* of the last row with `ts_time_get_nobegin_or_min()` when `start_isnull`. Please either make the boundary fix-up in `refresh.c` order-aware, or keep the list newest-first and process it in reverse here.
